# `Q-5-51` — Alias Redirect Skipped on a Case-Insensitive Output Directory

> `website.case-sensitive-paths: true` allowed an alias that differs
> from an existing file only by case, but the directory being
> rendered into treats the two as one file, so the redirect was not
> written.

## What this means

With `website.case-sensitive-paths: true` you have told Quarto that
the host your site is served from keeps `R/index.html` and
`r/index.html` apart, so an alias that differs from a page (or from
another alias) only by case is a redirect to write rather than a
[`Q-5-25`](Q-5-25.qmd) collision:

```yaml
# _quarto.yml
website:
  case-sensitive-paths: true

# r/index.qmd
aliases:
  - /R/           # the old URL, before the directory was renamed
```

That is true of the deployment target. It is not necessarily true of
the machine doing the rendering. On a default macOS or Windows
filesystem, `_site/R/index.html` and `_site/r/index.html` *are* one
file, and writing the redirect would replace the page with a redirect
— here, a redirect to itself.

Quarto checks the output directory before writing — by experiment,
not by operating system, since a macOS volume can be formatted either
way. When the directory folds case, the redirect is skipped and this
warning names it. The page is left intact. Everything else about the
render is unaffected, and on this machine the page already answers
for the redirect's URL, so nothing is missing locally.

When two *aliases* differ only by case, the one that sorts first is
written and the other is skipped.

## How to fix it

Nothing is wrong with the project. To produce the redirect, render on
a case-sensitive filesystem — typically the Linux CI job that builds
the published site. The output there contains both files.

If you did not mean to declare the host case-sensitive, remove
`website.case-sensitive-paths` and rename the alias so it differs from
the page by more than capitalization; see [`Q-5-25`](Q-5-25.qmd).

## Difference from Quarto 1

Quarto 1 has no such check and no such option. It compares paths
exactly, so on Linux it writes both files, and on macOS or Windows it
silently overwrites the page with the redirect. Quarto 2 never
overwrites the page: it either refuses the pair (`Q-5-25`, the
default) or, with `website.case-sensitive-paths: true`, writes the
redirect where the filesystem allows and warns where it does not.
